title: I finally understood why my options lost value even when Nifty moved my way. Now my algo filters trades on one number I used to completely ignore.
author: Electronic_Tea_2948
selftext:
This is the concept that quietly flipped how I think about options entirely.

I used to buy options purely on direction. I thought Nifty up means my call goes up, simple. So I would buy a call, Nifty would actually climb from 24,100 to 24,160, and my option would still be worth less than when I bought it. I genuinely could not understand how I was right and still losing.

The missing piece was implied volatility, basically how expensive options are at that moment based on how much movement people are expecting. When everyone is scared or an event is coming, options get pumped up and pricey. And here is the trap. I kept buying my calls when volatility was high and premiums were fat, usually right before big events, because that is when I felt the urge to trade. Then the event would pass, volatility would collapse, and even though Nifty moved my way a little, the air came out of my option faster than the price gain could help me. I was overpaying and then watching the premium deflate.

Once I understood this, I stopped trusting my gut on timing and let my algo handle it. Now my system checks where current volatility sits compared to its own recent history before it ever takes a trade. If volatility is already high and stretched, the algo knows buying options there is overpaying, so it either avoids it or looks to sell premium instead. If volatility is low and cheap, that is when buying makes more sense. The machine does not get excited and overpay like I did.

The big lesson. In options you are not just betting on direction, you are also buying or selling volatility, and the price you pay for that matters enormously. A number I used to ignore now sits at the center of every decision my system makes. Does anyone here build volatility filters into their entries, or still trade on price alone?
